findings.evidence: grep: `existsUnique_dynkinType_of_apply_mul_apply_eq_two` occurs outside its defining file only at FiniteType/Classification.lean:74, and that use is the `IsFiniteType.` version; the root-pairing version has no in-repo use. Its conclusion is character-for-character that of FiniteType/Classification.lean:130.
findings.fix: Delete the three root-pairing corollaries (the matrix-level `IsFiniteType.*` branch theorems are the ones actually consumed and should stay), or, if the branch information is wanted, strengthen each to state what its docstring claims, e.g. `∃! t, (t = .B _ ∨ t = .C _ ∨ t = .F4) ∧ t.Valid ∧ HasCartanType P b t`.
findings.issue: `TauCeti.existsUnique_dynkinType_of_apply_mul_apply_eq_two` (root-pairing) concludes exactly `∃! t, t.Valid ∧ HasCartanType P b t` — the same statement as the new `TauCeti.existsUnique_dynkinType` (FiniteType/Classification.lean:129) — but adds a double-edge hypothesis and yields nothing extra (`Nonempty ι` is derived from `u`, so the general theorem applies whenever this one does). It is dead, duplicated API. The same now holds for the pre-existing siblings `TauCeti.existsUnique_dynkinType_of_isSimplyLaced_of_degree_eq_three` (Star/Reindex.lean:376) and `TauCeti.existsUnique_dynkinType_of_isSimplyLaced_of_degree_le_two` (TypeA.lean:145), which this PR renders subsumed.

findings.evidence: Classification.lean:184-185 conclusion is `∃! t, t.Valid ∧ ∃ e, ∀ i j, A i j = t.cartanMatrix (e i) (e j)`, with no constraint on the constructor of `t`; the helper at line 145-173 produces `.B`/`.C`/`.F4` witnesses but the statement existentially forgets them.
findings.fix: Either add the disjunction `t = .B _ ∨ t = .C _ ∨ t = .F4` to the conclusion, or reword the docstring to say only that a unique valid type exists.
findings.issue: Docstrings assert "It is one of `Bₙ`, `Cₙ`, or `F₄`" (line 180, and line 204 for the root-pairing version) but the statements record no such restriction; the private helper `doubleEdgeCartanMatrix_existsUnique_dynkinType` establishes B/C/F4 and then discards it. A user reading the docstring gets an interface that does not deliver the advertised content.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn "isSimplyLaced_of" TauCeti/` returns no matches; `TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/FiniteType/Basic.lean` exposes `apply_mul_apply_mem_of_ne` (line 344) and friends but no simply-laced consequence.
findings.fix: Extract it as a public lemma next to the other `IsFiniteType` entry bounds, e.g. `theorem IsFiniteType.isSimplyLaced (h : IsFiniteType A) (h2 : ∀ i j, A i j * A j i ≠ 2) (h3 : ∀ i j, A i j * A j i ≠ 3) : A.IsSimplyLaced`, and use it here.
findings.issue: The step "a finite-type matrix with no entry product 2 or 3 is simply laced" is proved inline (25 lines, unfolding `Matrix.IsSimplyLaced` via `intro i j hij`). No such lemma exists in the repo, yet the public entry points `IsFiniteType.exists_equiv_forall_eq_cartanMatrix_A` (TypeA.lean:115) and `IsFiniteType.existsUnique_dynkinType_of_isSimplyLaced_of_degree_eq_three` (Star/Reindex.lean:341) both demand `hsl : A.IsSimplyLaced`, so every consumer must re-derive this proof.

summary: The new root-pairing corollary `existsUnique_dynkinType_of_apply_mul_apply_eq_two` is a strictly weaker duplicate of the top-level `existsUnique_dynkinType` added in the same PR (as are its two pre-existing siblings, now dead), and its docstring promises a type restriction the statement does not record. Separately, the simply-laced dichotomy the assembly needs is derived inline instead of being exposed as the missing `IsFiniteType` characteristic lemma that every public `hsl`-taking entry point requires.
